summary: Implemented the lotus-lean feature in the lane-a worktree: a closed lotus bud now leans toward the nearest fingertip (index/middle/ring/pinky/thumb) of any visible, active, dry, non-pinching, non-grabbing hand within 35 cm, easing in over 0.6 s and out over 1.2 s, with a warming halo (GLOW_GAIN_CLOSED + 0.14 * warmGlow while bloom < 0.25). The lean goes into the flower instance matrix as a base-pivot rotation (axis (leanZ, 0, -leanX)) composed with the yaw, and f.bud is recomputed from that rotation every frame before the touch test and glow update, so the touch target and halo follow the pod. A still fingertip 9–22 cm from the bud accumulates hoverT; at 0.6 s a 'lotusstir' event fires (thin rising band-passed white-noise whisper at 2x→3x the note's register-6 frequency in sfx.js) and at 2 s openFlower(i, { cause: 'patient', hand }) opens the bud; the FM bell for a patient bloom uses attack 0.06, dur 4.2, gain 0.40. openFlower now takes opts { cause, hand, openSeconds } and stores f.openSeconds (used by the 'opening' branch); the touch loop passes the hand whose tip hit; ctx.lotus.open(i, opts) passes opts through; 'lotusbloom' carries cause and hand. main.js logs 'lotusstir', summarizes 'cause', and world().lotus entries gain state and lean. Scenario gained three steps before the existing touch step (lotus-leans, lotus-patient-open, lotus-too-high-stays-closed) and parks the hand with curl 0.6 afterwards so the existing 'lotus-bloomed' step picks the next closed bud (cluster 1 at 1.44 m, inside its 2.2 m reach check; verified from the seeded layout). Verification was cut short by the orchestrator's output-enforcement: the harness run and a geometry probe were still executing when the structured result was demanded, and the scenario has not been run, so nothing is committed.

summary: Implemented Hush per the spec. A new ~110-line module src/world/hush.js (registered after fireflies, before leave) watches each hand for the pose (visible, active, open, still, not pinching/grabbing, palm normal.y < -0.8, palm joint within [-0.05, 0.03] m of the surface); after 0.6 s of hold a circle activates under the palm, its strength eases in (tau 0.8 s) and its radius grows from 0.25 m to 1.2 m over 3 s (ease-out cubic) while the centre follows the palm at 1/s; breaking the pose decays strength (tau 1.2 s) with r = max(r0, rGrown*s), and a pose resumed mid-fade continues growth from the current radius (no radius pop). It emits 'hush' {hand, pos} when s crosses 0.05 and 'hushend' {hand} below 0.02, and writes two vec4 arrays every frame (ctx.water.hush.data in tile uv for the sim, ctx.water.hushWorld in world metres for the surface) plus ctx.hush = {strength, circles, count}. wavesim.init allocates both arrays and the uHush uniform, the sim fragment damps velocity (x0.3) and height (x0.85 per step) inside the circles, and uDamping uses max(calm, 0.6*hush). water.js adds uHush, flattens the normal (x0.08), lifts fresnel to >= 0.32*hf so the sky comes through, darkens plankton (x0.1), draws a thin plankton-coloured ring on the spreading front, and uses the same calm max for uCalm. Sound: sfx plays a 6 s ceramic bowl on the chord root (C3-ish, 120 ms attack, half wet) plus a tuned bowl sample an octave up, and the calm drone gate includes hush strength; music gates raindrops on S.hushing (set by hush/hushend) with 3-7 s spacing. Hint 'rest a hand flat on the water and be still' appended (after 140 s, ready on touchedWater, done once a hush event has fired and strength >= 0.8 observed). main.js logs 'hush'/'hushend' and stats() gains hush. Four scenario steps were added after the fireflies step (hush-circle-forms, hush-stills-the-water, hush-dissolves, hush-no-new-draw-calls) with a control ripple before and the same ripple inside the disc after. Harness passed (0 errors, 60 XR draw calls, one pre-existing requestaborted warning for hands/left.glb); the scenario run had not finished when the orchestrator forced the result, so the new steps are unverified.

summary: Carrying a lantern to a closed lotus cluster and letting it go in the water now warms the bud open. In lanterns.js each record gains touched (set in onGrab, cleared in respawnFar) and amongPads; in the floating branch, after wind/walk/homing and before the hand-attraction term, the nearest ctx.lotus.clusters entry is found and within PADS.hold (0.40 m) vx/vz are damped to a quarter, so a placed lantern lingers while an open hand can still coax it out. In lotus.js a per-frame warmth pass (after the lean/bud pass, before the touch test) scans ctx.lanterns.list: floating, touched, settled, lit (bright > 0.3) lanterns within a 0.45/0.55 m hysteresis band accumulate f.warm (dt in, -2dt out, capped 3.5); past 2.5 s a closed bud opens via openFlower(i, { cause: 'lantern', openSeconds: 5 }) with a smaller energy bump (0.08) and softer ring (0.18), and while the lantern stays an open flower's timer is held at stay - 10 so it closes only 10 s after the lantern leaves. The brightest nearby lantern (any state but rising, within 0.6 m) is written to a new per-instance vec4 aLantern; the flower vertex shader computes vWarm (lambert toward the lantern with 1/(1+12d²) falloff) and the fragment shader adds amber (1.0, 0.70, 0.34)*0.9 to the petal and pod branches, so petals read amber on the lantern side and moon-pale on the other; the halo gains +0.10*smoothstep(warm) (mirror follows automatically). sfx.js onLotus plays a ceramic bell with a 0.35 s attack, dur 5, gain 0.32, wet 0.4 plus a 0.18 tuned-bowl layer for cause 'lantern'. hints.js gains 'leave a lantern among the lily pads' (after 130 s, ready when a lantern has been grabbed, a bud has bloomed and both are within reach; done on a lantern-caused bloom). main.js world().lanterns entries gain pads/touched. The scenario gained four steps after 'lotus-bloomed' (ready, grabbed, set-down, warms-lotus) and the bud opened 2.47 s after the splash, bloom 0.69 at +4 s, pads true. Harness PASS with 0 errors (60 XR draw calls, unchanged from the lane's previous run) and scenario PASS 21/21.

summary: An open, non-pinching, non-grasping hand now meets a floating lantern instead of passing through it. In src/world/lanterns.js a module-level nudgeContact(L, hands, ctx, t, dt) runs inside the floating branch after the attraction term and before head avoidance (skipped while dropping): for each visible/active hand whose palm is within 0.45 m, the 11 contact joints (wrist, middle metacarpal, four proximal phalanges, five tips) are tested as discs of radius j.radius+0.008 against the hull's 0.075 m flank in the band P.y-0.11 < j.y < top.y-0.02; the hull is moved out of the way positionally (never vertically), the world palm velocity's normal component feeds L.push (x0.9, capped 0.7 m/s, decays 1.5/s) and its tangential component feeds L.spinKick (clamped +-2.5 rad/s, decays 0.9/s). push is added to vx/vz every floating frame, heels the lean (leanT += push*0.5), flares the flame target to max(existing, 1+min(0.7, |push|*1.2)) while |push|>0.05, and spinKick adds to the yaw while floating. A fresh contact after a 0.25 s quiet gap guts the flame when the brush exceeded 0.35 m/s (bright = max(0.3, bright-0.2)), rings the water (0.1, 0.05+0.2*min(1,vn)), increments ctx.lanterns.touches and emits 'lanterntouch' {pos, hand, lantern, speed}. The hand attraction is now multiplied by smoothstep(ad, 0.095, 0.175) so a nuzzling lantern is not tugged into the fingers. sfx.js answers with a 900 Hz band-passed paper tap (dur 0.05-0.10 s, gain 0.03-0.13 with speed). main.js logs the event, exposes push on world().lanterns entries and lanternTouches in stats(). The scenario gained three steps after 'lantern-star' (lantern-nudge-ready, lantern-nudged, lantern-nudge-settles): a sideways brush at ~0.49 m/s pushed the lantern 0.24 m along -X with a 0.42 m/s touch, no pinch/grab/rig motion, and it was still floating with touches 1 afterwards. notesForIntegrator: Shared identifiers: NUDGE = { reach 0.45, skin 0.008, body 0.075, pushMax 0.7, pushK 0.9, spinK 2.5, spinMax 2.5, pushDecay 1.5, spinDecay 0.9, gutterSpeed 0.35, eventGap 0.25, attEaseNear 0.095, attEaseFar 0.175 } and CONTACT_JOINTS (module consts in lanterns.js); lanterns.js now imports TIP_NAMES from '../core/hands.js'. Lantern record fields added at spawn: push (THREE.Vector2, world m/s), spinKick (rad/s), touchT (-1e9), inContact (bool); reset in respawnFar and onGrab. ctx.lanterns.touches (count, initialised 0 in init). Function signature: nudgeContact(L, hands, ctx, t, dt) at module level next to stepPendulum; it mutates L.position.x/z, L.push, L.spinKick, L.bright, L.touchT, L.inContact and may emit 'lanterntouch' and call ctx.water.disturb. Update order in the floating branch is now: wind/walk/homing -> pads damping -> attraction (eased) -> push/spinKick decay -> nudgeContact (skipped while dropping) -> vx/vz += push -> flame target -> head avoidance -> lantern overlap -> integrate -> lean (leanT += push*0.5) -> bright easing. Yaw: L.yaw += (floating ? spin + spinKick : spin*0.4) * dt. Hand gate for contact: h.visible && h.active && !h.pinch.active && !h.grasp && !h.grabbed (open-ness is NOT required, unlike the attraction); velocity used is h.palm.velocity (world, includes rig velocity). main.js: 'lanterntouch' appended to the eventLog list after 'lanternstar'; world().lanterns entries now { x, y, z, state, pads, touched, push }; stats() gains lanternTouches (after lanterns). sfx.js: on('lanterntouch') -> noiseBurst bandpass 900 Hz q 1.2, dur 0.05+0.05*sp, gain 0.03+0.10*sp, sp = clamp(speed/0.8). Scenario: the new block sits between the 'lantern-star' block and the lotus-patience block, uses its own LN/L0 names (the outer const L is the star lantern), picks the nearest floating lantern by index from a fresh world(), and leaves the right hand parked at [0.25,1.25,-0.4] curl 0.6 like the later blocks; the lotus blocks re-read world() so the nudged lantern's new position does not matter to them (verified: lantern-lotus later grabbed lantern 1, not the nudged lantern 2). Fragile: the brush pose relies on the fake skeleton's fingertips sitting 0.175 m from the wrist along -X at yawDeg 90 and all joints lying within the flank band at wrist y = L.y+0.02; a feature that changes lantern float height, H, or hand joint radii should re-probe with tools/harness/out/lantern-nudge-probe.mjs (gitignored; 'skipStar' argument skips the 36 s star wait). Interplay: a lantern set down among the pads or attracted into an open hand fires a speed-0 lanterntouch on first contact (quiet tap). Any feature that makes hands touch floating lanterns (e.g. a hush disc or paddling near a hull) will now displace them and may fire lanterntouch; hands under the band (paddling, > 11 cm below the centre) and above the rim never push. Harness took ~14 min and the scenario ~45 min under concurrent lane load; run them detached (see tools/harness/out/nudge-launch.sh) rather than in a foreground call.
